horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build a field portfolio and seek junior roles in sustainable farming, organic agriculture, agricultural extension, and project support.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Choose soil health, water conservation, agroecology, climate-resilient agriculture, organic compliance, or farmer outreach.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead field programmes, coordinate technical teams, and evaluate sustainable farming projects.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine agricultural knowledge with climate adaptation, digital data, traceability, and programme evaluation.

blocks.text: Build a career helping farms adopt sustainable production methods through field assessments, soil and water management, farmer training, and evidence-based agricultural projects.

blocks.text: Sustainable Agriculture Officer

blocks.text: Sustainable agriculture, agroecology, environmental management, and rural development

blocks.label: Timeline assumption
blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a three-year undergraduate degree starting in 2026 and completing around 2029. If your university offers a four-year honours or research pathway, use the additional year for research, fieldwork, and postgraduate preparation. The exact course-to-career taxonomy mapping could not be verified, so this is a cluster-level roadmap.
These are planning horizons, not verified employment forecasts.

blocks.label: Four-year honours variant
blocks.text: Use Year 4 for a longer field study, supervised research, an advanced internship, or preparation for postgraduate study. Confirm the exact structure and eligibility requirements with your university.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Progress from recommending practices to measuring their results. Develop skills in climate-risk assessment, farm economics, digital field records, traceability, and monitoring and evaluation. Ground recommendations in local soil, rainfall, crops, and farmer economics.

PhD routes

blocks.label: Agroecology or sustainable agriculture
blocks.text: Farming systems, crop diversity, soil health, and environmental outcomes.

items.text: Soil science or natural-resource management: Nutrient cycling, soil quality, water conservation, and land management.

blocks.label: Climate-resilient agriculture
blocks.text: Drought adaptation, climate risks, and agricultural resilience.

items.text: Agricultural extension and rural development: Farmer adoption, livelihoods, programme design, and outreach.

blocks.label: Environmental science and sustainability
blocks.text: Ecosystem services, sustainability indicators, and food systems.
Verify the required master’s qualification, research proposal, supervisor availability, entrance process, and funding for each programme.

2040–2046: Aim to connect field evidence with programme and policy decisions. Keep learning about climate adaptation, sustainable production, traceability, and impact evaluation. Build a record of measurable results, such as improved water-use efficiency or soil-health indicators, and document the methods and limitations.
